Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question queue will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Technologies' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Voss, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Lee, Chief Security Officer; and Sarah Patel, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. SecureNet Technologies continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the third quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated SecureNet One Platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about NexusShield XDR 5.0 and the resulting acceleration in multi-product adoption is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: accelerating platform adoption over point products, mitigating the impact of currency fluctuations, maintaining low churn through superior customer success, driving performance in key product lines like cloud security and SASE, rolling out innovative product and feature launches, and fueling expansion within our existing large accounts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the third quarter was $1.35 billion, representing a 20% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 85% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 78%, while operating expenses were $920 million. Net income was $165 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.92. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper into the segment financials, I want to highlight a key strategic metric that's driving our outperformance: the accelerating shift in customer preference from legacy point products to our integrated SecureNet One Platform. This isn't just a numbers story—it's a validation of our platform-first strategy in a market where cybersecurity sprawl is the number one pain point for CISOs, with enterprises now juggling an average of 45 security tools, up from 30 just three years ago.

In Q3, our platform adoption rate—defined as the percentage of net new Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, attributable to SecureNet One, our AI-native XDR platform that unifies EDR, NDR, cloud workload protection, and SOAR capabilities—reached 72%, up from 58% in Q3 2023 and a sequential 68% in Q2. This marks the ninth straight quarter of double-digit year-over-year acceleration. For context, point products—our standalone modules like SecureNet Endpoint Shield or our legacy firewall add-ons—accounted for just 28% of net new ARR, down from 42% year-over-year. Overall, platform revenue now represents 81% of our total ARR of $1.42 billion, up 15 points year-over-year, while point product ARR share has compressed to 19%, reflecting a deliberate 22% year-over-year decline as we sunset non-strategic SKUs.

Why the momentum? First, the economics. Platform customers enjoy a 35% lower total cost of ownership versus multi-vendor point solutions, per our internal Forrester-style TEI study shared at Black Hat this year. This is evident in our metrics: average annual contract value for platform deals hit $1.2 million in Q3, 2.8 times higher than point products at $425,000. Dollar-based net retention for platform-only customers stands at 128%, versus 112% for mixed deployments—translating to $185 million in expansion ARR from existing platform users alone this quarter.

Segment-wise, enterprise adoption among Fortune 2000 equivalents led with 78% platform mix, fueled by our interoperability with leading data lakes for unified analytics. Mid-market, from 500 to 5,000 seats, clocked in at 65%, up 20 points year-over-year, thanks to our SecureNet One Essentials bundle, priced aggressively at $45 per endpoint per year with built-in MDR services—directly undercutting competitors at $55 to $60.

Regionally, the Americas remain our powerhouse at 75% platform adoption, representing 62% of total ARR growth, driven by U.S. federal mandates under CMMC 2.0 and the White House's zero-trust push. EMEA surged to 70%, up from 52% year-over-year, as NIS2 Directive compliance deadlines loom—we've closed 14 deals with major European firms, including a €28 million expansion with a leading German automaker moving away from point silos. APAC, our fastest grower at 42% year-over-year ARR increase, hit 62% platform mix, propelled by Singapore's cybersecurity levy and Japan's post-Log4Shell scrutiny; key wins include a JPY 5 billion platform migration at a top Tokyo bank, swapping legacy endpoints for our GenAI deception tech.

Technically, this shift is powered by our HyperThreat AI engine, now detecting 97% of zero-day exploits in under 90 seconds via federated learning across 15 billion daily events—outpacing peers in MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. Native integration with data platforms like Snowflake and ServiceNow for SIEM-less security data lakes has reduced alert fatigue by 68% in beta trials. Our Platform Migration Accelerator program has onboarded 320 customers year-to-date, delivering 4 times faster time-to-value than point rip-and-replace, with 92% converting to multi-module upsells within 12 months.

Strategically, this positions us uniquely in an $85 billion-plus endpoint and cloud security market growing at 18% CAGR. While point players struggle with net retention compression amid churn, our platform flywheel—bolstered by 135% net ARR expansion from modules like CloudGuard and DeceptionGrid—drives 142% dollar-based net expansion overall. Looking forward, we expect platform adoption to hit 78-82% by year-end, with remaining performance obligations from platform deals up 29% year-over-year to $2.1 billion, signaling multi-year visibility.

Before moving on, I also want to address a key factor influencing our top-line results: the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on revenue. As a global leader in next-generation cybersecurity platforms, we derive approximately 45% of our revenue from international markets. With our primary reporting currency in USD, currency volatility remains a material headwind or tailwind, particularly in a year marked by Fed rate hikes, ECB dovishness, and geopolitical tensions driving safe-haven flows into the dollar.

On a reported basis, Q3 revenue grew 20% year-over-year to $1.35 billion. However, on a constant currency basis—stripping out FX effects—that growth accelerates to 24%. Currency fluctuations created a $38 million, or 3.1% headwind to reported revenue, compared to a $12 million tailwind in Q3 2023 when the USD was weaker.

Regionally, EMEA, at 25% of revenue or about $338 million, faced the brunt at $22 million negative impact. The EUR depreciated 7.8% year-over-year against the USD, from 1.08 to 0.995, exacerbated by the ECB's slower rate path. Our DACH cluster saw EUR-denominated ARR bookings convert $15 million lower, while GBP exposure added another $5 million drag.

APAC, 20% of revenue or $270 million, saw a $14 million headwind, driven by JPY weakness down 12.5% to 148 per USD and AUD softening 5.3% to 0.67 per USD. Japan contributed $9 million of this. CNY stability limited China exposure drag to $2 million.

The Americas, 55% of revenue, were largely insulated, with minimal FX noise. About 60% of international revenue is transactional—billed in local currencies—making it sensitive to spot rates. Subscription revenue amplifies this, as multi-year contracts expose renewals to FX.

We're proactive: our FX hedging program covers 70% of forecasted 12-month transactional exposure using forwards and options, locking in $18 million of protection for Q4. We've accelerated local-currency invoicing to 65% of EMEA deals and implemented dynamic pricing in our SaaS platform that auto-adjusts for significant FX moves.

Volatility persists, with projections implying another 2-3% Q4 headwind, but we're tilting toward stable-currency pockets like LatAm and India. Long-term, consumption-based pricing in cloud security reduces FX beta by 15-20%.

Turning to customer metrics, specifically churn, which remains a cornerstone of our SaaS model. In the cybersecurity space, we measure success by sticky, high-value relationships that drive our industry-leading net retention rate.

For Q3, our gross dollar retention rate came in at 96.8%, translating to a quarterly logo churn rate of 3.9% and revenue churn of just 2.1%. Annualized, that's around 15% on logos and 8% on revenue—well below industry averages of 10-12% for logos and 5-7% for revenue. Our net revenue retention expanded to 118%, up 200 basis points quarter-over-quarter, fueled by 28% net expansion in our enterprise cohort through upsells like our XAI module for autonomous threat hunting.

This marks our fifth straight quarter of sequential churn improvement, down from 5.2% logo churn last year. Progress stems from macroeconomic stabilization—cyber budgets rebounding amid ransomware threats—and our retention initiatives.

Churn drivers: voluntary 85%, involuntary 10%, other 5%. Budget constraints and consolidation were 42% of voluntary churn, or 1.6% of ARR, hardest in mid-market. We've countered with our CyberStack Optimizer tool, reducing this by 35% year-over-year.

Product-market fit issues were 28%, mainly SMBs at 7.2% quarterly churn, with EMEA elevated at 5.1% tied to NIS2. Project ZeroTrust Bridge cut deployment time, yielding 22% churn reduction in beta accounts.

Competitive displacement was 18%, or 0.7% of ARR, hotspot in APAC at 4.8%. Our Partner Accelerator Program clawed back 15% of at-risk logos.

Performance gaps were 12%; our GenAI Response Engine slashed MTTR to 27 minutes, dropping this 50% quarter-over-quarter.

By segment: enterprise logo churn 1.8%, mid-market 4.5%, SMB 7.2%; US 3.2%, EMEA 5.1%, APAC 4.8%, all with year-over-year improvements and NRR from 105% to 122%.

Our Customer Success 2.0 framework boosted renewal NPS to 72. We're leaning into zero-trust convergence, with macro tailwinds like SEC rules and CISA profiles. We guide Q4 logo churn to 3.5-4.0%, NRR at 117%+.

As we execute on converged, cloud-native security, I'm pleased to provide a deep dive into our powerhouse product lines: Cloud Security and SASE. These represented 68% of bookings this quarter, driving much of our growth.

Cloud Security delivered $458 million in quarterly ARR—up 52% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter, our 11th straight quarter of 50%+ growth, fueled by multi-cloud migrations. Our CNAPP integrates CSPM, CWPP, and CASB, generating $285 million ARR, up 67%, blocking 12 million high-risk exposures.

We rolled out Aegis ShieldAI, reducing MTTR by 65%. Dollar net retention hit 128%, with expansions to DSPM. Americas led at 55%, EMEA 48%, APAC 62%. Partnerships position us as a CNAPP leader; we expect 55-60% growth in FY2025.

SASE posted $322 million ARR—up 68% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter—with 1,450 net new customers, including 12 deals over $5 million ACV. Secure traffic inspected reached 45 petabits monthly. Aegis Converge 3.0 cut latency by 40%, with 85% win rates in bake-offs.

APAC exploded 82%, EMEA 61%, Americas 52%. Net retention 135%, with bundling driving full-stack zero trust. We expect 70%+ growth as pipeline shifts.

These lines deliver 125% blended NRR and strong margins, positioning us for market share gains.

Finally, expansion within existing large accounts—over $1 million ARR—is a key driver. Our large account DBNER was 128%, up 300 basis points year-over-year, our 11th straight quarter above 120%. Of $156 million revenue growth, $52 million or 33% came from these expansions; we expanded 162 accounts by over 20%, 47 by 50%+.

Platform consolidation: a top global bank expanded 248% to $8.7 million ARR via CWPP and SASE integrations, cutting MTTR dramatically.

AI/ML innovations: 62% of expansions included GenAI Threat Hunting and ITDR.

North America 58% of expansions at 142% DBNER; EMEA 124%, APAC 135%. Churn under 2%. We expect Q4 at 130% with new orchestration.

This flywheel delivers predictable revenue.

Dr. Elena Voss: Thank you, Taylor. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing our HyperThreat AI for zero-day detection, native integrations for SIEM-less data lakes, and the Platform Migration Accelerator, alongside GenAI features like autonomous response and threat hunting that have slashed MTTR and boosted true positives to 98.7% in NexusShield XDR 5.0.

Marcus Lee: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware evolutions like LockBit 3.0 to AI-generated phishing up 250% and state-sponsored APTs—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with QuantumShield for post-quantum readiness and inline decryption in SASE.

Sarah Patel: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, expanding channel partnerships with MSSPs and hyperscalers to reach a wider audience, evidenced by wins in federal, DAX 40, and Tokyo banking, with 75% platform mix in Americas and surging APAC growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press * then 1 to join the queue. First question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Jamie Carter: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Taylor, you highlighted the FX headwind—can you elaborate on hedging effectiveness and Q4 outlook? Also, how does platform adoption influence your constant currency growth?

Taylor Kim: Thanks, Jamie. Our hedging covers 70% of exposure, locking in meaningful protection—$18 million for Q4 alone—and we've seen it mitigate about half the drag so far. Q4 headwinds should be 2-3%, or $25-30 million, but organic momentum more than offsets with 25%+ targets. Platform adoption directly boosts constant currency by emphasizing high-ACV, sticky deals less prone to FX volatility in renewals.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great results. Jordan or Taylor, on churn—any color on mid-market trends and how CyberStack Optimizer is performing? Also, expansion velocity in large accounts?

Jordan Hale: Lisa, thanks. Mid-market churn improved 120 basis points year-over-year to 4.5%, with our Optimizer tool driving 35% reduction in budget-related losses by benchmarking spends. Large account expansions hit 162 at 20%+, up 45% from last year, with DBNER at 128%—a flywheel from consolidation and AI upsells.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays.

Raj Patel: Elena, impressive on launches like SecureCloud SASE Elite and GenAI Hunter—how are these impacting CNAPP and SASE metrics, and competitive positioning?

Dr. Elena Voss: Raj, NexusShield XDR 5.0 and SecureCloud SASE Elite contributed $128 million new ARR, 22% of bookings. CNAPP ARR up 67% to $285 million, SASE 68% to $322 million, with 128-135% NRR. Our AI innovations score highest in waves from Forrester and Gartner, winning 85% bake-offs via low-latency eBPF and federated learning.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Torres with JPMorgan.

Mike Torres: Marcus, with threats escalating, how is SecureNet adapting post-quantum and supply chain risks? Tie to product performance if possible.

Marcus Lee: Mike, we're ahead with QuantumShield using NIST PQC standards like Kyber—60% enterprise adoption, boosting NRR 15 points. For supply chain, like SolarWinds echoes, our GenAI Response Engine covers 85% of platform, dropping MTTR to 27 minutes, integral to cloud security blocking 12 million exposures and SASE preventing 8.2 million lateral moves.

Jordan Hale: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
